text:
aya: Heads up — seeing tiny pods (0.25 GPU) bounce between nodes in eu-central during nightly scale-up. multiple evictions in last hour. Any idea? :thinking:
liam: yep saw that. Taint 'reserved-gpu: true' being applied on rack-drain, scheduler rebinds tiny pods repeatedly.
sumi: logs show preemption + backfill loop, kube-scheduler scoring favors newer nodes; pods small so get packed, then taint triggers eviction.
liam: can you paste a pod describe?
aya: ```kubectl describe pod tiny-train-xyz
Events:
  Type    Reason     Age   From               Message
  ----    ------     ----  ----               -------
  Normal  Scheduled  5m    default-scheduler  Successfully assigned default/tiny-train-xyz to node-eu-12
  Warning Preempted 4m    kubelet            Preempted by higher priority pod
  Warning Evicted    3m    kubelet            Node tainted: reserved-gpu:NoSchedule due to rack-maintenance
```
olivia: probably our taint application is async with node labeling. We recently tightened the taint controller to run on scale events.
sumi: two quick mitigations: 1) increase lease ttl on scheduler for tiny pods so they don't reschedule during transient taints; 2) add soft-affinity weight to prefer nodes with matching GPU shape to reduce fragmentation.
liam: agreed. Also can we try marking tiny pods as packable into warm-pool with soft-affinity to reduce churn? cost tradeoff but less evictions.
aya: I'll open a canary job to change lease to 30s and ramp for 2 hours.
olivia: ping @eng-sre for potential taint-controller restarts — want them aware.
eng-sre-bot: incident created: #INC-8123 tiny-pod pingpong eu-central, assignees: @olivia @liam
liam: quick note — if we add soft-affinity, watch for new fragmentation metric rising. measure: gpu_small_pod_pending_time and pack_fragmentation_ratio.
aya: thanks all, rolling now. will post results in 15m. :rocket:
